overview: Melvich Bay sits where the River Halladale reaches the north coast of Sutherland. The name comes from the Norse for 'sand dune bay', and it fits: a short walk through marram grass dunes leads to golden sand, sheltered by the pier at Portskerra to the west and the cliffs below Rubha an Tuir to the east.

It's on the North Coast 500 but most of the year it's very quiet. Look out for salmon jumping at the river mouth and seals in the bay; the village a few minutes away has toilets, a café, a shop and an inn. The A897 from Helmsdale through the Strath of Kildonan ends here, joining the A836 coast road, and the village has a well-known Gaelic choir.

The river feeds a sandbar that produces lefts and rights. That same river creates currents that change with rainfall and tide, and there are rocks to watch for, so it's a beach for confident intermediates rather than first-timers. Look at the river and the banks from the dunes before you paddle out, and give the river mouth a wide berth if the water is high.

text: Melvich is a river-mouth break with lefts and rights, picking up both local windswell and distant groundswell. North-west swell is ideal, and southerly winds blow offshore. Bigger swells may be needed to wrap fully into the bay.
It can work year-round, with autumn the strongest season and February often the best month. Water is cold, so bring a winter suit, hood, gloves and boots, and watch out for rocks.

Melvich is a river-mouth break with lefts and rights, best on a north-westerly swell with a southerly offshore. Watch out for rocks. It works all year, autumn best, and February can have clean waves a good share of the time.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Small beach car park
practical.text: Down a signed track from the main road through the village, then a short walk through the dunes.

practical.label: Facilities
practical.title: In the village
practical.text: Public toilets, a café, shop, post office and the Halladale Inn, a few minutes' walk away. No showers.

practical.label: Lifeguards
practical.title: None
practical.text: Call 999 or 112 and ask for the Coastguard in an emergency.

practical.label: Access
practical.title: Dunes and sand
practical.text: The dune path makes wheelchair access to the beach difficult.

practical.label: Check first
practical.title: Recent rain
practical.text: Heavy rain changes the river flow and the bank.

faqs.q: Where do I park for Melvich beach?
faqs.a: In the small car park down a signed track from the A836 through the village.
Not on your own. River currents and rocks make it better for confident intermediates.
